title: Scheme normalization has an isomorphism open over the isolated fibre points
statement: Let $h:X\to T$ be a separated morphism of finite type between schemes [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions]. Let $X\xrightarrow{i}C\xrightarrow{n}T$ be the concrete relative normalization of $T$ in $X$ [lem-weil-pbc-relative-normalization]. For $x\in X$, let $\xi_x$ be the unique point of the scheme fibre $X_{h(x)}$ mapping to $x$ [def-pc-scheme-fibre]. Put $I_h=\{x\in X:\{\xi_x\}\text{ is open in }X_{h(x)}\}$. There exists an open subscheme $O\subseteq C$ [def-weil-open-immersion] such that the induced map $i^{-1}(O)\to O$ is an isomorphism and the underlying subset of $i^{-1}(O)$ is exactly $I_h$. The inverse image has its induced open subscheme structure. No quasi-compactness or quasi-separatedness of $T$ is assumed.

source.place: Tag 03GW (lemma-finite-type-separated), equivalently phrased using isolated points of the scheme fibres.
